A 0–100 pre-breakout score for every stock • in a stock\'s detail, tap each part of \"How the score is made\" for its full working

How near the price is to its 20-day high, how tight and quiet the last 10 sessions\' base is, and where the close sits in the base. Distance is measured in the stock\'s own average daily range (ATR), so small and large stocks weigh the same.
Price above rising 20- and 50-day averages (DMA), and the 20 DMA above the 50 DMA.
Today\'s relative volume (RVOL) and how dry volume was in the 5 sessions before — quiet first, then a burst.
How many rupees traded on average each day over the last 20 sessions — more turnover, easier entry and exit.
The 5- and 20-day return. Trend already counts this, so it weighs less.
STRONG = %1$s+ (about the market\'s top 7–8%%) • WATCH = %2$s+ • below that WEAK.
Today\'s volume ÷ the last 20 sessions\' average. At %1$s× or more the card shows a volume spike.

Entry = the 20-day high + 0.1 ATR (confirming the breakout). Stop = the 10-day low, kept between 1 and 2 ATR. Targets = 1.5, 2.5 and 4 times the risk (1.5R / 2.5R / 4R). Each target shows about how many days: targets as many ATRs from the entry, when they were hit in NSE\'s past data, were usually hit within that many trading days of the entry — an estimate, not a guarantee. The quick target (0.75R) is hit more often before Target 1, and the wide stop (1.5R) protects it more but the loss is bigger. Breakouts hold better when breakout-day volume is 2× the average or more; with yesterday\'s score STRONG on top, \"🎯 High-probability\". The percentages are from the last year of NSE data, not a guarantee.
NEW = new in the top list since the last scan • ▲ / ▼ = how far the rank rose/fell since the last scan • ★ = your watchlist.
This app is for information and learning only, not investment advice. Do your own research and manage your risk before every trade.
Stock lists: NSE (main board and SME) and BSE bhavcopy • Shares: NSE • Daily prices: Yahoo Finance. Data may be a little delayed.
